title: A number over 50 characters is refused while on an open part request
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), with 'Part Library & Inventory → View / Create & Edit / Delete' and See Financial Data.
  • Part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-LONG-01) is stocked at {Location-A}.
  • Work order {Work-order-1} (for example S2-15444) has a line, {Line-1} (for example "Replace - Brake pot"), with an open part request for {Part-A}: requested and not received.
  • Part {Part-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-LONG-02) is stocked at {Location-A} and is on no part request.
  • {Number-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-LONG-01-XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX) is exactly 51 characters long, and {Number-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-LONG-02-YYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYY) is exactly 60 characters long. Neither is used by any part.
custom_steps:
1. Type {Part-A} in the Inventory search.
  2. Click the {Part-A} row.
  3. Replace the Part Number with {Number-A}.
  4. Click Save.
  5. Click Cancel.
  6. Type {Part-B} in the search.
  7. Click the {Part-B} row.
  8. Replace the Part Number with {Number-B}.
  9. Click Save.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 4: nothing is saved and the window stays open. A red message reads "Part number can't be longer than 50 characters while it's on an open part request.", with the second, smaller line "Please try to resolve this." It goes away after about 3 seconds.
  • Step 5: the window closes, and {Part-A} keeps its number.
  • Step 9: {Part-B} saves with the 60-character number {Number-B}, because it is on no open part request.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, as edited 9 Oct 2026 (Ready for dev), S13-N7, §8 User Feedback Summary, read 13 Oct 2026; design canvas: no board shows this behaviour (13 Oct copy). Tech plan §6 Phase 6 functional tests. Source-verified 13 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Part Lifecycle QA build exists).
